summary: Gateway AI is validating options between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Primary interest is Dedicated reserved GPUs with an ability to burst to shared capacity. Key concerns: tenant isolation, preemption risk, burst latency, KMS/encryption, and clear unit pricing for hot vs cold tokens. Agreed next steps: pricing scenarios, security docs, sample-trace benchmark, and a technical deep dive on isolation and preemption.
questions: How does Redwood handle noisy neighbor on dedicated pools?
What guarantees exist for burst capacity and fallback?
How are hot token/unit costs calculated with batching and KV cache?
What is the private (VPC) onboarding timeline?
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-02-25
- Time: 16:00 PT
- Duration: 43 minutes
- Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lina Gomez (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Gateway VP Eng), Devon Hart (Gateway SRE), Priya Shah (Gateway ML Platform), Omar Lee (Gateway CTO)

AUTO SUMMARY (auto):
Gateway wants to reserve a baseline dedicated GPU pool for inference critical workloads, but keep the ability to burst for unpredictable traffic. They care a lot about tenant isolation (no co-tenancy on the same GPU if possible), fallback behavior when reserved pool is saturated, and encryption/KMS auditability. They will send request traces and want a short benchmark.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining uh this is Samir from Redwood, lina's with me from solutions. we're excited to walk through how dedicated reserved capacity could look for Gateway. can i do a quick 1-2 min intro from your side?
[00:14] Marta: sure, great thanks. i'm marta, vp engineering. we've got production inference for chat summarization and multi-turn retrieval -- some realtime and some async workloads. we're looking at options because Hosted is hitting cost and latency tradeoffs.
[00:29] Devon: devon here we run the SRE side, we care about tail latency and how preemptions or node sharing would affect SLAs.
[00:39] Priya: priya on ML platform, main ask is predictable throughput for certain models and isolation for PII-sensitive flows. also curious about kv cache behavior across tenants.
[00:48] Lina: thanks. quick context from our side, Redwood Dedicated gives you a dedicated GPU pool you reserve, with autoscaling and optional burst to our shared pools. you can also run a Private deployment if you need a customer-managed plane but that generally adds a couple weeks to onboarding.
[01:06] Omar: couple quick constraints: legal wants single-tenant for those PII flows; ops wants ability to burst in ecomm spikes; budget prefers a mixed approach rather than full private.
[01:19] Samir: got it. two axes: isolation vs elasticity. we commonly see customers reserve a baseline of nodes sized to 95th percentile steady state, then enable burst for brief spikes. question for you: how long are your spikes and what's acceptable degradation?
[01:33] Devon: spikes are usually short — 3 to 10 minutes — but can have sudden 10x delta. we can tolerate slightly higher latencies for non-critical flows but critical flows need <120ms 95th for generate requests.
[01:46] Priya: and for PII flows we'd prefer no co-tenancy on GPU level. is dedicated pool strictly single-tenant?
[01:54] Lina: dedicated pools are tenant-isolated at the pool level, not always at the sole GPU card level unless you choose node fencing. we offer 'segregated nodes' option where the reserved nodes are pinned to your tenant only — that meets single-tenant requirements but increases cost.
[02:10] Marta: what's the preemption behavior when you burst to shared and capacity's constrained? do requests queue or failover to a smaller model?
[02:18] Samir: good question. our smart routing will try preferred path: reserved pool -> warmpool prewarmed nodes -> shared burst. if burst is saturated, we have automatic fallback policies: either route to a quantized variant or lower-cost model, or queue briefly up to a configured timeout. you pick fallback policy per route.
[02:34] Devon: does that mean a request could be served by a different model variant mid-session? that might break downstream consistency.
[02:41] Lina: we recommend sticky sessions for multi-turn chat. you can pin a session to a model variant, but if you want graceful degradation we support structured reroutes with a notice header. there are tradeoffs.
[02:54] Marta: what about KV cache? priya mentioned it — is it shared? i.e. could another tenant evict our prefix cache?
[03:02] Samir: KV cache is per-model instance. for Dedicated pools the KV cache is partitioned by tenant session, but on shared burst you can get cold starts. node fencing ensures cache locality. we also support persistent prefix cache for warm pools for your sessions — reduces cold-token overhead.
[03:20] Priya: ok that sounds promising — can you quantify cost delta for node fencing vs shared-pool with warmpool?
[03:27] Samir: rough ballpark — node fencing can add ~25-40% to baseline reserved cost depending on GPU type and utilization patterns; warm-pool prewarm/keepalive is cheaper but doesn't guarantee exclusive hardware. i'll put exact numbers in the pricing doc.
[03:40] Devon: what about preemption at cloud provider level, e.g., if nodes are preemptible or spot-like? we need clear SLAs.
[03:48] Lina: our Dedicated offering uses guaranteed instances for reserved pools, not spot. burst capacity can include pooled capacity which may use a mix; we surface expected latency tiers and we can set an allowed fallback to higher-latency handling rather than letting it error. reserved capacity comes with SLA for uptime and basic latency SLOs.
[04:06] Omar: encryption — do you support customer-managed KMS and HSM? and are audit logs available per request?
[04:13] Samir: yes both. we integrate with major KMS providers and offer HSM for Private deployments; audit logs and request-level metadata are available in Redwood Console, can be forwarded to customer's SIEM. we'll attach SOC2 and encryption docs.
[04:27] Marta: timeline — if we decide to pilot, how fast can you get dedicated nodes provisioned?
[04:33] Lina: provisioning baseline reserved pool typically 7-14 days depending on GPU availability and region. Private/VPC adds extra steps — usually 3-6 weeks. if you need a rapid pilot we can start on Hosted with a configured Dedicated-looking profile to validate routing and fallbacks, then swap onto reserved GPUs when provisioned.
[04:52] Devon: bench question — we run a pattern with mixed short generates and long-context 4k sequences. how should we structure the benchmark?
[04:59] Samir: best is to provide a 48h representative trace — capture sequence length distribution, QPS, and percentiles. we'll run both continuous batching and KV-cache-enabled runs to show delta. can you provide that?
[05:12] Devon: yes we can. i'll upload it.
[05:15] Priya: are there any rate shaping or tenant-level quotas we can set to avoid noisy-neighbor impacts?
[05:21] Lina: yes you can set per-tenant rate limits, soft quotas, and emergency circuit breakers. there's also an autoscale policy for dedicated pools to scale within min/max bounds.
[05:33] Marta: i want to dig into cost model — how are tokens priced when batching and caching are used? i've seen billed tokens vary across vendors and it's opaque.
[05:41] Samir: good point. Redwood bills on consumed tokens but we break down at the route level: raw model tokens, cache hits (which are cheaper), and prefetch overheads. when batching, cost per token typically drops because of amortized compute, but we surface per-token latency and per-route unit economics so you can decide. we'll include worked examples in the pricing doc.
[06:00] Omar: any limitations for long-running KV cache warmups when switching models? we occasionally change model weights for A/B and want to avoid cold starts.
[06:08] Lina: you can pin prewarmed model variants; our rollout tooling supports canary warmups and background KV population. for heavier transitions we recommend rolling warmups during off-peak windows.
[06:20] Marta: what about hybrid: private control plane but use Redwood's shared inference hardware? is that supported?
[06:26] Samir: yes, that's our common hybrid pattern — private control plane with VPC peering, keys remain customer-managed but model execution can be on Redwood-hosted nodes. it's a middle ground for compliance + flexibility.
[06:36] Devon: metrics and observability — will we get token-level latency, cache hit rates, and per-request traces?
[06:42] Lina: yes token-level cost and latency, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks that correlate with your APM. we can also add specific alerts for cache miss rates or fallback events.
[06:53] Marta: ok let's talk pilot scope — what would you propose for a 6-8 week pilot to validate both perf and isolation?
[07:00] Samir: propose: week 0-1: confirm trace and pilot routes, week 2: provision reserved baseline (or simulate on Hosted if you need faster), week 3: run benchmarks and KV cache tests, week 4-5: run real-traffic canary with 10% traffic, week 6: review metrics + iterate on fallback policies. deliverables: benchmark report, landing cost model, and runbook.
[07:22] Priya: that sounds doable. legal will need the SOC2 docs and a short runbook about data residency and logs.
[07:29] Samir: we'll attach those. Lina, anything to add about technical deep dive?
[07:34] Lina: yes i'd like to spend the deep dive on: node-fencing internals, behavioral preemption scenarios, and KV cache partitioning details. we'll demo fallback routing logs and a short simulation.
[07:46] Devon: can we include a test that simulates 10x spike and observes tail latencies and fallback triggers?
[07:52] Lina: absolutely — that's part of the benchmark plan.
[07:55] Marta: are there examples of customers who chose mixed reserved + burst with node-fencing? i'd like references.
[08:02] Samir: we can share anonymized case notes — i'll include a short reference sheet, but nothing identifiable.
[08:09] Omar: quick budget check — what's the minimum commit you'd recommend to be meaningful?
[08:14] Samir: typically we see customers start with enough to cover 50-70% of steady state to get predictable economics and keep smaller burst allowance; a tiled example will be in the pricing scenarios.
[08:25] Priya: any compliance gotchas for HIPAA/PHI flows?
[08:28] Lina: we have HIPAA-compliant paths via Dedicated + Private combos, plus required BAAs. we'll surface the checklist.
[08:36] Marta: great. let's recap next steps.
[08:39] Samir: recap: samir sends pricing scenarios and T&Cs, lina sends technical deep dive invite and warmpool notes, devon uploads trace, marta confirms stakeholders and legal contacts. target follow-up 2025-03-04 to finalize pilot.
[08:56] Devon: noted. uploading trace today.
[08:59] Priya: thanks everyone.
[09:01] Samir: thanks all, we'll follow up with docs.
